page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2681.48, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average range. The stress-ng multi-core score is 10764.32, and the uncached memory read bandwidth is 69.61 GB/sec. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU extended instructions, both of which rank in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance local storage or GPU acceleration. It is appropriate for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference, where its average memory bandwidth and strong single-core performance can be leveraged effectively.
